newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Philips pulls plug on Superclub.
newsitem.headline: Philips pulls plug on Superclub.

text.p: Philips Electronics NV said on Wednesday it had decided to wind up the activities of its subsidiary Superclub on April 1.
"This decision was inevitable because the size of the continuous losses made further operations irresponsible," Philips said in a statement.
Superclub is a chain of shops selling and renting videotapes and selling audio CDs, computer games and multi-media entertainment packages such as CD-interactive and CD-Rom.

Philips said Superclub had suffered the losses because turnover per outlet was insufficient, margins were too low, costs were too high and the market for videotapes and CDs had been disappointing. It did not specify the extent of the losses.
Until April 1 of this year, Superclub's entire inventories will be offered to clients in a special closing down sale, Philips said.

Superclub is headquartered in the Belgian town of Bornem and has 540 employees, who were informed of the closure today. The chain operates a total of 87 shops, 61 of which are in Belgium, 22 in the Netherlands and four in France.
